name: The mitotic cell cycle and DNA replication

questions.q: What are the primary sequential phases that comprise the standard eukaryotic cell cycle?
a: Mitosis, Meiosis, Binary Fission, and Apoptosis

questions.q: During which specific sub-phase of interphase does replication of nuclear DNA occur?
What major cellular events characterize prophase of mitosis?
a: Chromosomes align individually at the cell equator
Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles
Chromosomes condense and become visible, nuclear envelope breaks down, and spindle fibers begin to form from centrosomes
Daughter nuclei reform and DNA decondenses

questions.q: During which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate at the centromere and migrate toward opposite spindle poles?
What is the biological significance of mitosis in multicellular eukaryotic organisms?
a: Growth, tissue repair, asexual reproduction, and cell replacement
Production of haploid genetic gametes for sexual fertilization
Reduction of chromosome number by half

questions.q: Which semi-conservative model enzyme is responsible for unwinding and unzipping the DNA double helix during replication by breaking hydrogen bonds?
What is the function of DNA polymerase during DNA replication?
a: Sealing nicks in the sugar-phosphate backbone
Catalyzing the addition of free deoxynucleotide triphosphates to the 3' end of a growing polynucleotide strand using complementary base pairing

questions.q: What is a telomere, and what is its role in eukaryotic chromosomes?
a: The central point where sister chromatids attach
An enzyme that degrades damaged DNA
The site where transcription initiation begins
A repetitive nucleotide sequence at the ends of linear chromosomes that protects vital coding DNA from degradation during successive cell divisions

questions.q: What mechanism of DNA replication was proven by the Meselson-Stahl experiment using nitrogen isotopes ($^{14}N$ and $^{15}N$)?
Which checkpoint in the cell cycle assesses whether DNA replication during the $S$ phase was successfully and completely finished before the cell enters mitosis?
What structural event defines metaphase of mitosis?
a: Nuclear envelopes reform around separated chromatids
Chromosomes align along the equator (metaphase plate) of the spindle apparatus
Centromeres divide and pull poles apart

questions.q: What occurs during cytokinesis in animal cells compared to plant cells?
a: A rigid cell plate forms across the center
Animal cells undergo furrowing via a contractile ring of actin and myosin filaments, whereas plant cells form a cell plate from Golgi vesicles

questions.q: What is the role of DNA ligase during DNA replication?
a: Joining Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand by catalyzing phosphodiester bond formation
Unwinding supercoils ahead of the replication fork

questions.q: Which enzyme synthesizes short RNA primers required to provide a free 3'-OH group for DNA polymerase attachment during replication?
Why is the lagging strand synthesized discontinuously in short segments (Okazaki fragments) during DNA replication?
a: Because DNA polymerase can only synthesize new strands in the 3' to 5' direction
Because RNA primers inhibit continuous polymerization
Because DNA polymerase operates exclusively in the 5' to 3' direction, and the template strand runs 5' to 3' away from the replication fork
Because nucleotides run out during synthesis

questions.q: What term describes an abnormal, uncontrolled mass of cells resulting from mutations in genes regulating the cell cycle and division?
What are proto-oncogenes, and how can they contribute to cancer development when mutated?
a: Normal genes that stimulate cell division; mutations can turn them into oncogenes that cause hyperactive, uncontrolled cell proliferation
Genes that trigger programmed cell death exclusively
Enzymes that repair ultraviolet radiation damage
Proteins that condense chromosomes during prophase

questions.q: Which tumor suppressor protein acts as a critical checkpoint guardian, halting the cell cycle or triggering apoptosis if DNA is severely damaged?
What is the function of cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases (CDKs) in the eukaryotic cell cycle?
a: Regulating the progression of the cell cycle through various checkpoints by phosphorylating target proteins

questions.q: What morphological change characterizes telophase of mitosis?
a: Chromosomes condense and spindle fibers form
Nuclear envelopes reform around two sets of chromosomes, nucleoli reappear, and chromosomes uncoil

questions.q: What is the precise definition of a gene mutation?
a: A permanent, random change in the nucleotide base sequence of DNA
An accidental error in RNA translation
The normal duplication of chromosomes during interphase

questions.q: Which type of mutation involves the insertion or deletion of one or more nucleotide base pairs, shifting the reading frame of triplets during translation?
What is the biological outcome of a 'silent' base-substitution mutation?
a: It causes immediate cell death due to protein truncation
It alters the amino acid sequence of the resulting protein significantly
It changes a codon into a different codon that encodes the exact same amino acid, due to the degeneracy of the genetic code

questions.q: Which chromosomal aberration occurs when a segment of a chromosome breaks off, inverts 180 degrees, and reinserts?
What is the primary function of centromeres during mitosis?
a: Holding sister chromatids together and serving as the attachment site for spindle microtubule kinetochores
Forming the cell plate during plant cytokinesis

questions.q: Which protein molecules form the core complexes around which nuclear DNA is wound to create nucleosomes and chromatin fibers?
What defines semi-conservative DNA replication?
a: Both original strands are completely degraded and replaced by new molecules
The resulting DNA molecules consist entirely of newly synthesized parental fragments
Each newly synthesized DNA molecule consists of one original (parental) strand and one newly synthesized complementary strand
DNA replication occurs only in every second cell cycle

questions.q: What is apoptosis, and what role does it play in multicellular organisms?
a: Uncontrolled cancerous cell division leading to metastasis
Accidental cell death caused by physical trauma or infection
The normal synthesis of proteins during interphase
Programmed cell death controlled by specific biochemical pathways, essential for development and removing damaged cells

questions.q: What is the role of topoisomerase during DNA replication?
a: Relieving torsional strain and supercoiling ahead of the advancing replication fork
Binding single-stranded DNA to prevent re-annealing

questions.q: Which nitrogenous bases are classified as double-ring purines found in DNA molecules?
What is the function of single-stranded binding proteins (SSBs) during DNA replication?
a: Breaking hydrogen bonds between base pairs
Binding to newly separated single strands of DNA to prevent them from re-annealing into a double helix before replication occurs

questions.q: What occurs during the $G_1$ phase of interphase?
a: Rapid DNA replication and histone synthesis
Cell growth, synthesis of organelles, and high metabolic activity including protein synthesis and ATP production

questions.q: Which checkpoint ensures that all chromosomes are properly attached to spindle microtubules at the metaphase plate before anaphase begins?
What is the consequence of a nonsense point mutation in a structural gene?
a: It changes an amino acid to a chemically similar one
It introduces a premature stop codon, resulting in a truncated, typically non-functional protein
It has zero effect on the final polypeptide product
It alters the reading frame of all subsequent codons

questions.q: What role does telomerase play in specialized cells such as germ cells and stem cells?
a: It accelerates cellular aging and programmed cell death
It induces random mutations in somatic tissues
It extends or maintains telomere length, preventing chromosomal shortening and allowing continued cell division
It acts as a restriction enzyme breaking DNA

questions.q: Which phase of the cell cycle represents a quiescent resting state where cells exit the active cycle and cease dividing (e.g., mature neurons)?
What is the principal difference between chromatin and chromosomes?
a: Chromatin is the relaxed, uncoiled form of DNA-histone complexes during interphase; chromosomes are highly condensed, coiled structures visible during mitosis
Chromatin contains RNA; chromosomes contain only lipids
Chromatin is found in prokaryotes; chromosomes in eukaryotes

questions.q: Which enzyme is responsible for proofreading newly synthesized DNA strands and removing mismatched nucleotides via 3' to 5' exonuclease activity?
What is the significance of the leading strand being synthesized continuously during DNA replication?
a: It runs in the 3' to 5' direction away from the fork
Because DNA polymerase reads the template 3' to 5' and synthesizes the new strand continuously in the 5' to 3' direction toward the replication fork
It is synthesized slower than the lagging strand

questions.q: Which environmental mutagenic agent causes the formation of covalent thymine dimers in DNA strands, disrupting replication?
